quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Which safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts to protect you in a front crash. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belt.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane with no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, whether there is a marked crosswalk or not. Always stop and let them finish crossing safely.

questions.question: What can impair your ability to drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness all reduce your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: Which actions are unlawful?

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass in no passing zones, at railroad crossings, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, in work zones, or when a vehicle ahead has stopped for a pedestrian.

questions.question: You miss your exit on an interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back.
Roll down your window and ask another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Instead, go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road.
Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause collisions with other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) increases, you become:
questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Follow traffic signals unless a police officer is directing traffic. When an officer is present, follow their directions instead of the signal.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has limited height. Do not continue if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce alcohol in your blood. They may keep you awake, but they do not make you sober.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move on.
questions.explanation: Do not take road rage personally. When another driver cuts you off, stay calm and keep driving safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either one.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, reduces caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, slow down for turns and curves. This is more important than on dry roads.

questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that pulls your attention away from the road. Distractions can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: Drivers who have drunk alcohol:

options.text: Always know the dangers they face.
Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles well.
Are better drivers because they focus more.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles well.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and body. It harms your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no car is in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Stop and let them cross safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the light. Protect pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol and drugs can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs together can make both effects stronger. It is very dangerous to drive after using either one. It is even more dangerous to use both.

questions.question: What is the only medically proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?

options.text: Wait for your body to process it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process it.
questions.explanation: Alcohol leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol content (BAC). Only time will lower your BAC.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down and look for a train when you see a railroad crossing sign. Be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not drive around the gate.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress makes it hard to concentrate. Wait to drive until you feel calm.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, drive to the next rest stop to take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills are not a good solution and may make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your turn or exit, you should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even when no other cars are visible.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy night traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. Make this a habit every time.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when:

options.text: You see a stop sign at an intersection.
A traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and when a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. This is used where visibility is poor and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to yield to oncoming traffic when turning left at a green light. Complete your turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead, usually a few hundred feet away. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.
